help_probe.stdout:
Usage: simms skysim [OPTIONS] MS

  Predict model visibilities from a sky model into an MS.

Options:
  -as, --ascii-sky TEXT           Catalogue of sources. See the documentation
                                  for accepted units.
  -fs, --fits-sky TEXT            FITS file (or directory of Stokes cubes)
                                  containing the sky model.
  -ws, --wsclean-sky TEXT         WSClean component list (point and Gaussian
                                  components, Stokes I).
  -fsi, --fits-sky-interp [nearest|linear|cubic]
                                  Interpolation method when the MS and FITS
                                  frequency grids do not match and the cube is
                                  kept.
  -pol, --polarisation / --no-polarisation
                                  Simulate all available Stokes parameters. If
                                  false, only Stokes I.
  --pol-basis [linear|circular]   Polarization basis for the simulation.
  -pt, --pixel-tol FLOAT          Minimum brightness for a pixel to be
                                  considered in direct Fourier transform.
  -fsp, --fits-spectrum [auto|flat|poly|cube]
                                  How the FITS sky model varies with
                                  frequency.
  --fits-spi TEXT                 Spectral-index (and higher-order)
                                  coefficient maps, ordered c1, c2, ...
                                  Requires --fits-ref-freq.
  -frf, --fits-ref-freq FLOAT     Reference frequency (Hz) of an analytic FITS
                                  spectrum. Defaults to the MS band centre.
  --fits-spectrum-order INTEGER   Order of the fitted log-polynomial spectrum.
                                  1 is a plain spectral index.
  --predict-backend [auto|dft|fft|perchan]
                                  Backend for FITS sky model prediction.
  --fft-precision [single|double]
                                  Precision of the FFT calculation.
  --do-wstacking / --no-do-wstacking
                                  Whether to use w-stacking for FFT-based
                                  visibility prediction.
  -ad, --ascii-delimiter TEXT     Delimiter used in the ascii-sky.
  -col, --column TEXT             Data column for simulation.
  --nworkers INTEGER              Number of workers (one per CPU).
  -rcs, --row-chunks, --rowchunks INTEGER
                                  Maximum number of rows per chunk. Controls
                                  the row-wise task/memory granularity; the
                                  effective size is reduced when needed so
                                  every worker gets several chunks.
  -ccs, --chan-chunks INTEGER     Number of channels per chunk. Defaults to
                                  all channels in one chunk.
  -pb, --primary-beam TEXT        Beam model config: a simms beam-config YAML
                                  mapping each ANTENNA telescope name to a
                                  beam model, or a Cattery/DDFacet
                                  heterogeneous-beam json (--Beam-FITSFile
                                  json form, keyed by ANTENNA.NAME) if the
                                  path ends in .json. For Cattery/DDFacet
                                  beams a circular-correlation MS may be used
                                  when --beam-jones full is selected.
  --beam-band [UHF|L]             Default band for JimBeam entries that omit
                                  an explicit model/CSV.
  --beam-pa-step FLOAT            Spacing (degrees) of the parallactic-angle
                                  grid the beam is sampled on.
  --beam-grid-max-gib FLOAT       Hard ceiling (GiB) on the sampled beam grid
                                  held in memory for the whole run; pointing
                                  errors add 2 (first) or 3 (laplacian)
                                  derivative grids of the same size.
  --beam-jones [diagonal|full]    Primary-beam application: per-feed voltage
                                  or full 2x2 E-Jones.
  -fbm, --fits-beam-mode [aterm|average]
                                  Primary-beam handling for the FITS-image
                                  path: 'aterm' applies exact per-antenna
                                  a-terms in the image domain (time- and
                                  frequency-interpolated, heterogeneity-
                                  aware); 'average' multiplies the sky by a
                                  single PA-averaged power beam (legacy
                                  approximation).
  -aft, --aterm-freq-tol FLOAT    Largest allowed error (in voltage-beam
                                  units, beam peak ~1) of the a-term's linear-
                                  in-frequency interpolation between knot
                                  channels. Smaller means more frequency
                                  knots; 0 or negative samples the beam at
                                  every channel.
  -tnc, --telescope-name-column TEXT
                                  ANTENNA-table column holding the per-antenna
                                  telescope/type label that maps to a beam
                                  model.
  -bla, --beam-l-axis [-X|X]      Sign convention for a Cattery/DDFacet .json
                                  primary-beam config's L axis; ignored for
                                  YAML beam configs, which specify their own
                                  axis convention. Matches DDFacet's --Beam-
                                  FITSLAxis.
  -bma, --beam-m-axis [Y|-Y]      Sign convention for a Cattery/DDFacet .json
                                  primary-beam config's M axis; ignored for
                                  YAML beam configs, which specify their own
                                  axis convention. Matches DDFacet's --Beam-
                                  FITSMAxis.
  --smearing [analytic|subsample|none]
                                  Time and bandwidth smearing of the predicted
                                  model. 'analytic' (default) applies the sinc
                                  decorrelation implied by the MS's own
                                  CHAN_WIDTH and EXPOSURE, so the model
                                  matches averaged data instead of over-
                                  predicting sources far from the phase centre
                                  on long baselines -- but only the per-
                                  visibility (ASCII, WSClean and FITS
                                  --predict-backend dft) paths can carry it,
                                  and the FITS gridder backends warn and
                                  predict unsmeared. 'subsample' additionally
                                  smears the gridder backends by averaging
                                  whole predictions over sub-times and sub-
                                  frequencies (a ~1%% method; cost multiplies
                                  with the sub-sample counts, chosen
                                  automatically and capped by --smearing-
                                  subsamples), while the per-visibility paths
                                  keep the analytic factor. 'none' predicts a
                                  monochromatic, instantaneous model
                                  everywhere.
  -sss, --smearing-subsamples INTEGER
                                  Cap on the automatically chosen per-axis
                                  (time and frequency) sub-sample counts under
                                  --smearing subsample; capped runs warn with
                                  the residual amplitude bias. No effect for
                                  other --smearing modes.
  -fi, --field-id INTEGER         Field ID.
  --spw-id INTEGER                Spectral Window ID.
  --sefd FLOAT                    Add noise using this SEFD value.
  --seed-noise INTEGER            Random seed for the thermal noise. Omit for
                                  a non-reproducible run. The realisation also
                                  depends on the row chunking, which
                                  --nworkers feeds into, so reproducing a
                                  previous run needs the same --seed-noise,
                                  --row-chunks and --nworkers. This is the
                                  renamed --seed; the same value gives the
                                  same noise.
  --seed-gains INTEGER            Random seed for the corruption terms' random
                                  phases/matrices and the pointing-error
                                  draws. Omit for a deterministic per-label
                                  draw; the thermal noise stream is unaffected
                                  either way.
  --seed INTEGER                  Deprecated alias for --seed-noise; --seed-
                                  noise wins if both are given.
  --corruptions TEXT              YAML file describing RIME corruptions:
                                  antenna 'gains' applied to the predicted
                                  visibilities and/or antenna 'pointing'
                                  errors, which are applied through the
                                  primary beam (--ascii-sky with --primary-
                                  beam only).
  -asp, --ascii-species [bdsf_gaul|bdsf_srl|aegean|wsclean]
                                  Non-simms sky model type.
  -ic, --input-column TEXT        Column that 'add'/'subtract' combine the
                                  simulation with. Defaults to --column.
  --mode [sim|add|subtract]       How the simulation reaches --column: 'sim'
                                  overwrites it, 'add' adds the simulation to
                                  --input-column, 'subtract' subtracts it from
                                  --input-column. --input-column defaults to
                                  --column.
  --source-schema TEXT            Custom source schema (YAML) mapping columns
                                  in a custom sky model to the columns simms
                                  expects.
  --help                          Show this message and exit.
